text:
Stop reading marketing advice from people who haven't shipped in a decade.

Most of what you've been told about "great copy" was written for a Mad Men world that doesn't exist anymore. Your reader has 280 milliseconds before they bounce. Your buyer trusts a stranger on TikTok more than a McKinsey deck. The CMO who hired the agency that wrote your hero — they were optimising for a 2015 attention curve.

Here's what actually works in 2026:

1. Name the shadow before they do. Whatever they're afraid of — the silent fear behind the click — say it first. Disarms defence in one move.
2. One specific number beats every adjective. "Increased revenue" lands at zero. "Cut churn from 8.4% to 3.1% in 90 days" lands at 100.
3. Write for the LLM AND the human. The buyer's next click is "what does Claude say about X." If your page isn't structured for citation, you don't exist.

Try this for your next launch. Then DM me the headline.
